'''Alessandra Buonanno''' (born 1968)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.balzan.org/en/prizewinners/alessandra-buonanno-and-thibault-damour/bio-bibliography|title=Alessandra Buonanno and Thibault Damour 2021 Balzan Prize for Gravitation: Physical and Astrophysical Aspects|date=February 2024}}</ref> is an [[Italian-American]] theoretical physicist and director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics]] (Albert Einstein Institute)<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=New director at the Albert Einstein Institute: Prof. Alessandra Buonanno has accepted position at the Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics in Potsdam, Germany|url=https://www.aei.mpg.de/1129045/New_Director_AB|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160918203957/http://www.aei.mpg.de/1129045/New_Director_AB |archive-date=18 September 2016 |access-date=8 June 2020|website=Press release of the Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics, 16 January 2014}}</ref> in [[Potsdam]]. She is the head of the "Astrophysical and Cosmological Relativity" department.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Astrophysical and Cosmological Relativity (Potsdam)|url=https://www.aei.mpg.de/astro-cosmo-rel|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180908103244/http://www.aei.mpg.de/astro-cosmo-rel|archive-date=8 September 2018|access-date=8 June 2020|website=Webpage of A. Buonanno's division at the Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics}}</ref> She holds a research professorship<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Suplee|first=Anne|date=|title=Buonanno, Alessandra – UMD Physics|url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/people/faculty/current/item/67-buonanno.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919122318/http://umdphysics.umd.edu/people/faculty/current/item/67-buonanno.html |archive-date=19 September 2015 |access-date=8 June 2020|website=Webpage of A. Buonanno at the University of Maryland|language=en-us}}</ref> at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]], and honorary professorships at the Humboldt University in Berlin,<ref>{{Cite web|last=gilse|title=Special Colloquium for the Awarding of an Honorary Professorship to Prof. Dr. Alessandra Buonanno (Albert Einstein Institute, Potsdam) — Department of Physics|url=https://www.physik.hu-berlin.de/en/kolloquium-en/colloquia/sonderkolloquium-zur-verleihung-einer-honorarprofessur-an-prof-dr-alessandra-buonanno-albert-einstein-institut-potsdam|access-date=8 June 2020|website=www.physik.hu-berlin.de|language=en}}</ref> and the University of Potsdam.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Universität Potsdam – Institut für Physik und Astronomie|url=http://www.physik.uni-potsdam.de/index.php?&people_id=595&m=visitenkarte,self|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200608175923/http://www.physik.uni-potsdam.de/index.php?&people_id=595&m=visitenkarte,self |archive-date=8 June 2020 |access-date=8 June 2020|website=Contact information of A. Buonanno on Potsdam University webpage}}</ref> She is a leading member of the [[LIGO Scientific Collaboration]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=LIGO Scientific Collaboration Directory|url=https://roster.ligo.org/roster.php?do=roster&search=group&target=86|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200728123651/https://roster.ligo.org/roster.php?do=roster&search=group&target=86 |archive-date=28 July 2020 |access-date=28 July 2020|website=A. Buonanno's LIGO group in the LSC member roster}}</ref> which observed gravitational waves from a binary black-hole merger in 2015.<ref name="GW150914">{{cite journal |last1=Abbot|first1=B.P.|title=Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |date=2016 |volume=116 |issue=6 |article-number=061102 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.061102 |pmid=26918975|arxiv=1602.03837|bibcode=2016PhRvL.116f1102A|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Buonanno earned her MSc in 1993, and she completed her PhD in theoretical physics at the [[University of Pisa]] in 1996.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=DFG, German Research Foundation – Prof. Dr. Alessandra Buonanno|url=https://www.dfg.de/en/funded_projects/prizewinners/leibniz_prize/2018/buonanno/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180203025349/http://www.dfg.de/en/funded_projects/prizewinners/leibniz_prize/2018/buonanno/index.html|archive-date=3 February 2018|access-date=8 June 2020|website=Website of the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft about A. Buonanno}}</ref> After a brief period spent at the theory division of [[CERN]], she held a postdoctoral position at the [[Institut des Hautes Etudes Scientifiques]] (IHES) in France and the R.C. Tolman Prize Fellowship at the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Postdoctoral Fellows of the Burke Institute|url=https://burkeinstitute.caltech.edu/people/postdoctoral-fellows|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200803090103/http://burkeinstitute.caltech.edu/people/postdoctoral-fellows |archive-date=3 August 2020 |access-date=8 June 2020|website=List of postdoctoral fellows at Burke Institute/Caltech}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
Buonanno became a permanent researcher (Chargée de 1ere classe, CR1) in 2001 at the [[Institut d'astrophysique de Paris|Institut d'Astrophysique de Paris]] (IAP) and then at the [[Astroparticle and Cosmology Laboratory]] (APC) in Paris with the [[Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique]] (CNRS) before joining the University of Maryland as a physics professor in 2005.<ref name=":0" /> She moved to the Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Buonanno, Alessandra|url=https://www.mpg.de/7698804/gravitationsphysik_wissM4|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628072757/http://www.mpg.de/7698804/gravitationsphysik_wissM4|archive-date=28 June 2015|access-date=8 June 2020|website=A. Buonanno on the Max Planck Society's website|language=en}}</ref>

Buonanno was a Kavli Fellow at the [[Kavli Frontiers of Science]] Japanese-American Symposium of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alessandra Buonanno|url=http://www.nasonline.org/programs/kavli-frontiers-of-science/frontiers-alumni/alumni-directory/alessandra-buonanno.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210820125555/http://www.nasonline.org/programs/kavli-frontiers-of-science/frontiers-alumni/alumni-directory/alessandra-buonanno.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 August 2021|access-date=2021-08-20|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> She was the William and Flora Hewlett Fellow at the [[Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study]] at [[Harvard University]], from 2011 to 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alessandra Buonanno|url=https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/people/alessandra-buonanno|access-date=2021-08-20|website=Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University|language=en}}</ref> She was a Distinguished Visiting Research Chair at the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics|Perimeter Institute]] from 2014 to 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Reports and audits {{!}} Perimeter Institute|url=https://perimeterinstitute.ca/reports-and-audits|access-date=2021-08-20|website=perimeterinstitute.ca}}</ref>

Buonanno's work with [[Thibault Damour]] of reducing the two-body problem in general relativity to an [[effective one-body formalism]],<ref name="EOB">{{cite journal |last1=Buonanno |first1=Alessandra |last2=Damour |first2=Thibault |title=Effective-one-body approach to general relativistic two-body dynamics |journal=Phys. Rev. D |date=1999 |volume=59 |issue=8 |article-number=084006 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.59.084006 |arxiv=gr-qc/9811091 |bibcode=1999PhRvD..59h4006B |hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0019-8ADF-8 |s2cid=14951569 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.59.084006}}</ref><ref name="inspiral-plunge">{{cite journal |last1=Buonanno |first1=Alessandra |last2=Damour |first2=Thibault |title=Transition from inspiral to plunge in binary black hole coalescences |journal=Phys. Rev. D |date=2000 |volume=62 |issue=60415 |article-number=064015 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.62.064015 |arxiv=gr-qc/0001013 |bibcode=2000PhRvD..62f4015B |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.62.064015|hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0019-8AD4-D |s2cid=18247018 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>  and her research at the intersection of analytical-relativity modeling<ref name="inspiral-merger-ringdown">{{cite journal |last1=Buonanno |first1=Alessandra |last2=Cook |first2=G. |last3=Pretorius |first3=F. |title=Inspiral, merger and ring-down of equal-mass black-hole binary |journal=Phys. Rev. D |date=2007 |volume=75 |article-number=124018 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.75.124018 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.75.124018|arxiv=gr-qc/0610122 |bibcode=2007PhRvD..75l4018B |s2cid=53578705 }}</ref><ref name="improved-EOB">{{cite journal |last1=Barausse |first1=E. |last2=Buonanno |first2=Alessandra |title=An improved effective-one-body Hamiltonian for spinning black-hole binaries |journal=Phys. Rev. D |date=2010 |volume=81 |issue=64024 |article-number=084024 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.81.084024 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.81.084024|arxiv=0912.3517 |bibcode=2010PhRvD..81h4024B |s2cid=119102991 }}</ref><ref name="EOB-generic">{{cite journal |last1=Taracchini|first1=A. |title=Effective-one-body model for black-hole binaries with generic mass ratios and spins |journal=Phys. Rev. D |date=2014 |volume=89 |issue=61502 |article-number=061502 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.89.061502 |arxiv=1311.2544 |bibcode=2014PhRvD..89f1502T |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.89.061502|hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0023-F6AF-7 |s2cid=32703759 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> and [[numerical relativity]] simulations were employed to observe [[gravitational waves]] from merging binary black holes for the first time, and infer their astrophysical and cosmological properties.<ref name="GW150914" /><ref name="Tests-GR">{{cite journal |last1=Abbot|first1=B.P. |title=Tests of general relativity with GW150914 |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |date=2016 |volume=116 |issue=22 |article-number=221101 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.221101 |pmid=27314708 |arxiv=1602.03841 |bibcode=2016PhRvL.116v1101A |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="GW151226">{{cite journal |last1=Abbot|first1=B.P. |title=GW151226: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a 22-Solar-Mass Binary Black-Hole Coalescence |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |date=2016 |volume=116 |article-number=241103 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.241103 |pmid=27367379 |arxiv=1606.04855 |bibcode=2016PhRvL.116x1103A |doi-access=free }}</ref> Beyond her core expertise in modeling gravitational waves from compact-object binary systems, Buonanno, in collaboration with Yanbei Chen, computed the quantum-optical noise in the advanced-[[LIGO]] gravitational-wave detectors,<ref name="Qnoise">{{cite journal |last1=Buonanno |first1=Alessandra |last2=Chen |first2=Yanbei |title=Quantum noise in second generation, signal recycled laser interferometric gravitational wave detectors |journal=Phys. Rev. D |date=2001 |volume=64 |issue=42006 |article-number=042006 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.64.042006 |arxiv=gr-qc/0102012 |bibcode=2001PhRvD..64d2006B |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.64.042006|hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0019-84A2-2 |s2cid=9280888 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref name="signal-recycle">{{cite journal |last1=Buonanno |first1=Alessandra |last2=Chen |first2=Yanbei |title=Signal recycled laser interferometer gravitational wave detectors as optical springs |journal=Phys. Rev. D |date=2002 |volume=65 |issue=42001 |article-number=042001 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.65.042001 |arxiv=gr-qc/0107021 |bibcode=2002PhRvD..65d2001B |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.65.042001|hdl=11858/00-001M-0000-0018-FEFA-1 |s2cid=10231808 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> and showed that quantum correlations between photon shot noise and radiation-pressure noise (i.e., the optical-spring effect) can circumvent constraints imposed by the Heisenberg uncertainty principle in those detectors.{{citation needed|date=August 2021}}

== Awards and honors ==
* 2023: Buonanno received the [[Oskar Klein Medal]] by [[Stockholm University]] and the Nobel Committee of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] and gave the [[Oskar Klein Memorial Lecture]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=About the centre - Oskar Klein Centre |url=http://www.okc.albanova.se/about-the-centre?open-collapse-boxes=ccbd-oskarkleinmemoriallecture,ccbd-thisyearslecture |access-date=2023-11-30 |website=www.okc.albanova.se |language=en}}</ref>
* 2023: Elected Member of the [[Accademia nazionale dei Lincei|Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]] (Italian National Academy of Sciences)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buonanno, Alessandra {{!}} Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei |url=https://www.lincei.it/it/content/buonanno-alessandra |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=www.lincei.it |language=it}}</ref>
* 2022: [[Tomalla Foundation|Tomalla Prize]] for her "outstanding work on gravitational-wave physics"<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alessandra Buonanno receives the 2022 Tomalla Prize |url=https://www.aei.mpg.de/790105/alessandra-buonanno-receives-the-2022-tomalla-prize |access-date=2022-10-10 |website=www.aei.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Tomalla Prize ceremony at the University of Geneva – 14 October |url=https://home.cern/news/announcement/cern/tomalla-prize-ceremony-university-geneva-14-october |access-date=2022-10-10 |website=CERN |language=en}}</ref>
* 2021: [[Balzan Prize]] in the subject area "Gravitation: physical and astrophysical aspects" (shared with [[Thibault Damour]])<ref name="Milano Zurigo">{{cite web | title=THE 2021 BALZAN PRIZEWINNERS | website=Milano Zurigo | url=https://www.balzan.org/en/news/thw-2021-balzan-prizewinners | access-date=15 December 2021 | archive-date=26 January 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126231057/https://www.balzan.org/en/news/thw-2021-balzan-prizewinners | url-status=dead }}</ref>
